release_notes.prompt.copilot:
Summarize the commits below as release notes.

Rules:
- One line per item, 40 characters or fewer
- End each item with a noun phrase
- No file names, function names, prefixes, issue numbers or URLs
- Write only changes that users can notice
- Leave out internal refactoring, tests and docs
- Merge similar items into one
- At most 4 items per category
- Output only the format below, with no explanation or preamble

Format:
**New features**
* Add settings diagnostics

**Bug fixes**
* Fix logs being cut off

**Improvements**
* Add a hint for the run history location

Commits:
{commits}

Turn the following commits into user-facing release notes in English. No file names, prefixes, issue numbers or URLs. Group them under 'New features', 'Bug fixes' and 'Improvements':

dispatch.comment.title: ⚠️ **Could not run the follow-up workflows of this release automatically**
dispatch.comment.intro:
This repository has no PAT (`_GITHUB_PAT_TOKEN`), so after the release merge the follow-up
workflows are started directly. Every one of those calls failed.
dispatch.comment.check_permissions: - Repository Settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions is set to `Read and write permissions`
dispatch.comment.check_manual_run: - Running the workflows above manually from the Actions tab (Run workflow) applies this release

build_trigger.source_error.body:
❌ **App build trigger failed**

{error}

**How to fix:**
- Building from a PR: write the comment on the PR page.
- Building from an issue: the issue needs a "{signature}" comment.
  - That comment must contain a `{heading}` section with the branch name.
- Or name the branch directly in your comment: `@projectops app build <branch-name>`
